c.tagline: The gateway city to Slovakia's soaring High Tatras.

taxi.fareNote: Ride-hailing coverage is limited in Poprad — Bolt operates but with few drivers, so local taxis remain the reliable option. Confirm the meter is on or agree a price in advance.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number reaching police, fire, and ambulance; mountain rescue in the Tatras is 18 300.

hood_desc: The lively heart of Poprad along Námestie sv. Egídia, a long pedestrian square lined with pastel houses, cafes, shops and the town church; close to the train and bus stations and the departure point for the High Tatras, it is the most convenient base.

Poprad's best-preserved historic quarter, a medieval square of Renaissance burgher houses and the St George church founded by German colonists; the prettiest and most atmospheric place to stay, minutes from AquaCity.
A large, modern residential district south of the centre with apartment blocks, shopping, the ice stadium and everyday amenities; practical and well-priced rather than scenic.
The geothermal AquaCity resort and the wooded Kvetnica valley on the town's edge, built around thermal pools, spa hotels and forest walks; a relaxed nature-and-wellness base under the Tatras.
A former standalone town now a quiet historic suburb of Poprad, with its own church, square and small-town feel; a calm, local area a short ride from the centre.
lodging: DOMA u nás Boutique hotel & spa

water.note: Tap water is safe — Tatra mountain water is excellent.

transit.hours: City buses run from roughly 5:00 AM to around 11:00 PM; the Tatra Electric Railway (TEŽ) up to the mountain resorts runs from early morning until late evening.
transit.note: Poprad is compact and walkable. City buses (MHD Poprad) cover the town, while the narrow-gauge Tatra Electric Railway (TEŽ) from Poprad-Tatry links the city to Starý Smokovec, Štrbské Pleso and the High Tatra resorts.
transit.pay: Buy bus tickets in cash from the driver or with a transit card; TEŽ mountain-railway tickets are sold at stations, machines and online, and regional TATRY travel passes cover multiple days.

train: Poprad-Tatry station on the main Bratislava–Košice line ( ZSSK )

transit.m: City bus to the centre (~15 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving ~10% for good service is customary and appreciated.

food.name: Bryndzove halusky
food.desc: Slovakia's national dish: soft potato dumplings folded through tangy sheep's bryndza cheese and scattered with crisp bacon and its fat.

places.name: Koliba u Stefana
places.note: Rustic timber koliba locals name first for halusky and grilled mountain meats.

places.name: Halusky Bistro
places.note: Small bistro built around halusky, with strapacky and pirohy variations too.

places.name: Koliba Kamzik
places.note: Open fire, folk interior and generous portions; popular with Tatras-bound families.

food.name: Kapustnica
food.desc: Thick sauerkraut soup with smoked pork, klobasa sausage, dried mushrooms and sometimes prunes. Mountain fuel served all winter in a bread bowl.

places.name: Koliba u Stefana

places.name: Restauracia Atrium
places.note: Tatras hotel dining room a short train ride up; hearty Slovak staples after hiking.

places.name: Sabato

food.name: Grilled ostiepok
food.desc: Smoked, hand-moulded sheep's cheese from Tatra shepherd huts, grilled until it squeaks and served with cranberry jam.

places.name: Koliba Kamzik

places.name: Koliba u Stefana

places.name: Koliba u Stefana

food.desc: Venison goulash slow-cooked with juniper, red wine and root vegetables, served with bread dumplings. Classic Tatra hunting-country cooking.

places.name: Koliba Kamzik
places.note: Game stews and grilled meats in a chalet setting; strong winter menu.

places.name: Sabato

places.name: Koliba u Stefana

food.name: Sulance s makom
food.desc: Finger-shaped potato dumplings rolled in ground poppy seed, sugar and melted butter. The everyday Slovak sweet finish, also made with walnuts.

places.name: Halusky Bistro

places.name: Sabato

food.desc: Warm, slightly sour sheep whey left over from making bryndza, drunk by the cup at shepherd huts and kolibas. Best in the summer grazing season.

landmarks: Spisska Sobota
This astonishingly intact medieval quarter of Poprad clusters Renaissance burgher houses around St. George's Church and its carved altar by Master Pavol of Levoca.
Church of St. Egidius
Poprad's 13th-century Gothic church on the main square hides medieval frescoes, including one of the oldest known depictions of the High Tatras.
St. Egidius Square
Pastel Renaissance and burgher facades line Poprad's long central square, a pleasant promenade with the snowcapped High Tatras rising directly behind.
AquaCity Poprad
Geothermal water from deep underground feeds this award-winning aquapark's pools and saunas, steaming outdoors against a spectacular Tatra mountain backdrop.
Tatra Gallery
A converted early-1900s steam power station on the river showcases contemporary Slovak art beneath its atmospheric industrial steel trusses.
Podtatranske Museum
One of Slovakia's oldest museums stars the extraordinary 4th-century wooden chamber tomb of a Germanic prince unearthed beneath Poprad in 2006.
Strbske Pleso
The Tatra Electric Railway climbs from Poprad to this glacial lake resort, whose mirror-still waters reflect two-thousand-meter granite peaks.
Lomnicky stit Cable Car
From nearby Tatranska Lomnica, a dramatic cable car soars to Slovakia's second-highest summit at 2,634 meters for dizzying panoramic visits.
Belianska Cave
The High Tatras' only show cave winds past pagoda-like stalagmites and calcite waterfalls in the mountains near Tatranska Kotlina.
Evangelical Church of the Holy Spirit
A Neo-Gothic Lutheran church standing beside St. Egidius's Square, its tall spire a defining feature of Poprad's historic skyline.

train.note: Poprad-Tatry station is the gateway to the High Tatras and sits right in the centre of town, with the narrow-gauge Tatra Electric Railway (TEŽ) leaving from its own platforms for Starý Smokovec and Štrbské Pleso. The station is on the Bratislava-Žilina-Košice main line, so IC and EuroCity trains reach Bratislava in about 4 hours and Košice in around 1.5, and the same corridor carries the through trains from Prague, including RegioJet's overnight service with couchettes and a sleeper. Three operators compete on Prague-Poprad and there is no single booking site: compare RegioJet, Leo Express and ZSSK/CD separately, since each sells only its own seats and the cheapest fares go early. Slovak residents travel free on ZSSK, which fills trains fast, so reserve a seat wherever the option is offered.

intl.to: Prague & Brno (Czechia), Kraków & Zakopane (Poland), Vienna (Austria), Budapest (Hungary)

bus.note: The bus station is immediately beside the railway station, which makes interchange painless. FlixBus and RegioJet handle the international coaches, mostly overnight to Prague in around 8 hours plus daytime runs over the mountains to Kraków and Zakopane; both sell online, and RegioJet coaches come with steward service and free drinks. Domestic buses run by SAD Poprad reach the villages, the Slovak Paradise and trailheads the trains do not serve, with tickets from the driver in cash or by card. Slovakia, Czechia, Poland, Austria and Hungary are all in Schengen, so there are no border checks on any of these routes.

ferry.note: Poprad is landlocked at the foot of the High Tatras, roughly 400 km from the nearest sea, and the Poprad river through the town is a shallow mountain stream, so no ferry or scheduled boat service exists.

half.name: Spis Castle
half.blurb: One of Central Europe's largest castle ruins, UNESCO-listed and brooding atop a travertine hill, lies an easy drive east of Poprad.
